record.context_brief: Zero-counting limits for complex orthogonal polynomials
record.original_question: Let V be an external field on C, meaning a continuous function V : C -> R union {+infinity}, not identically +infinity, such that lim_{|z| -> infinity} (V(z) - log(1 + |z|)) = +infinity. For each n, let P_n be the unique monic polynomial of degree n satisfying the orthogonality relations integral_C P_n(z) z^k e^{-n V(z)} dA(z) = 0 for k = 0, 1, ..., n - 1, and let nu(P_n) be its normalized zero counting measure. Find external fields V for which nu(P_n) converges weakly to a limit measure mu_V as n -> infinity, and characterize the limiting measure mu_V.

evidence.quote: Let P be a monic polynomial of degree n with zeros z1, ..., zn, listed according multiplicities. We use nu(P) = 1/n sum_j delta_{z_j} to denote the normalized zero counting measure of P.

An external field on C is a continuous function V : C -> R union {+infinity}, not identically +infinity, with lim_{|z|->infinity} (V(z) - log(1 + |z|)) = +infinity. The growth condition guarantees that, for each n, there is a unique monic polynomial Pn of degree n such that integral_C Pn(z) z^k e^{-nV(z)} dA(z) = 0, k = 0, 1, ..., n - 1.

Problem. Find external fields V such that the sequence of normalized zero counting measures of the orthogonal polynomials (2) has a weak limit, say nu(Pn) -> mu_V as n -> infinity, and characterize the limiting measure mu_V.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let dA denote the area (Lebesgue) measure on the complex plane C. An external field on C is a continuous function V : C → R ∪ {+∞}, not identically +∞, satisfying the growth condition
  lim_{|z|→∞} ( V(z) − log(1 + |z|) ) = +∞.

For every nonnegative integer n, this growth condition ensures the existence of a unique monic polynomial P_n of degree n satisfying the non-Hermitian planar orthogonality relations
  ∫_C P_n(z) z^k e^{−n V(z)} dA(z) = 0,  k = 0, 1, …, n − 1.

For a monic polynomial P of degree n with zeros z_1, …, z_n (counted with multiplicity), let
  ν(P) := (1/n) Σ_{j=1}^n δ_{z_j}
denote its normalized zero counting measure.

Problem. Determine those external fields V for which the sequence (ν(P_n))_{n≥1} converges weakly to a probability measure μ_V on C as n → ∞, and provide an explicit characterization (e.g. as a potential-theoretic equilibrium / S-curve measure) of the limiting measure μ_V in terms of V.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of identifying external fields V on C for which the zeros of non-Hermitian planar orthogonal polynomials have a weak limit, and characterizing that limit, remains open. Partial results exist for specific classes (polynomial/Gaussian-type perturbations, trefoil weights, S-curve constructions), where the limiting zero distribution is described via equilibrium measures on S-curves and Riemann–Hilbert/steepest descent analysis, but no complete characterization is known for general V.

status_evidence.title: Non-Hermitian Orthogonal Polynomials on a Trefoil
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic analysis of non-Hermitian orthogonal polynomials uses the Deift/Zhou steepest descent analysis, with zeros distributing on critical trajectories of a quadratic differential according to the equilibrium measure in an external field.
status_evidence.claim: Only special classes of external fields have been fully analyzed; the general characterization is not established.

status_evidence.title: Orthogonal Polynomials and S-curves (arXiv:1112.5713)
status_evidence.snippet: The limit zero distribution is presented by an equilibrium measure of an S-curve associated with the problem if such a curve exists.
status_evidence.claim: Limit zero distributions are characterized via S-curves when these exist, indicating partial progress rather than a full solution.

status_evidence.title: Discontinuity in the Asymptotic Behavior of Planar Orthogonal Polynomials Under a Perturbation of the Gaussian Weight
status_evidence.snippet: Studies asymptotics of planar orthogonal polynomials under specific Gaussian perturbations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to address case-specific external fields, indicating the general problem is still open.
